content: Would CSLib benefit from a formalization of Gold's theorem?
Generally it helps us all if you state the theorem or link to a suitable formalisation of it. We come from diverse backgrounds
You need active learning models for this.

Oh. Do you mean the by request mode of learning mentioned in the wiki article? Gold's Identification is often proved on passive learning otherwise. In my understanding, the theorem is more about text presentation than the learner and the request mode does not expand what is learnable over the passive learners.
The main result argues for unlearnability over positive only text presentations.
The theorem says that not even regular languages are learnable with any learner given text presentation (positive only labels), while context sensitive languages (even primitive recursive!) are learnable with informant presentation (informant presentation has positive and negative labels)
I find the proof creative, it uses an ordering argument (with superfinite class assumption and a locking construction) to prove the unlearnability.
